info.text: Unit 19 — Writing a defect report in Simplified Technical English. Listening, reading, use of English (obligatory articles + bank terms), and vocabulary.

name.text: L1 · Dialogue 1 — report vs shift note

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again (From shift note to defect report). What makes a defect report different from a shift note?

generalfeedback.text: A defect report is a formal record, so every word must be an approved word with one meaning. That is what removes ambiguity.

answer.text: It uses approved words with one meaning.

feedback.text: Correct — approved words, each with one meaning, remove ambiguity.

answer.text: It is written quickly at the end of every shift.

feedback.text: No — that describes the rough shift note, not the report.

answer.text: It records the technician's personal opinion of the part.

feedback.text: No — a report states checkable facts, not opinions or guesses.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The mentor says the words seemed and might are good words for a defect report.

generalfeedback.text: False. "Seemed" and "might" give ambiguity. You write what you saw, not what you guessed.

feedback.text: No — those words are guesses, and an inspector cannot check a guess.
Correct — they create ambiguity, so STE avoids them.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again (Write the procedure in STE). What is a procedural sentence?

generalfeedback.text: Each step is a procedural sentence — a command in the active voice that starts with a technical verb.

answer.text: A command in the active voice.

feedback.text: Correct — one instruction, active voice, starting with a technical verb.

answer.text: A long description of the whole repair task.

feedback.text: No — a procedural sentence gives exactly one step.

answer.text: A passive note about what should be done.

feedback.text: No — STE uses the active voice, not the passive.

name.text: L4 · Dialogue 2 — nouns in a cluster

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The mentor says that a certain number of nouns together create ambiguity (a noun cluster). How many nouns together?

generalfeedback.text: Three. "Three nouns together create ambiguity." Break the cluster into the technical name plus small words.

feedback.text: Correct — three nouns in a row is a noun cluster.
The mentor says three nouns together create ambiguity.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogues 1 and 2 again. How many ideas (or instructions) should you put in each short sentence?

generalfeedback.text: One. "Put one idea in each short sentence" and "one clear instruction in each line."

feedback.text: Correct — one idea, or one instruction, per sentence.
The speakers say one idea, or one instruction, per line.

name.text: L6 · Dialogue 3 — where the warning goes

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again (Peer review before sign-off). The warning about the live circuit should come before the step.

generalfeedback.text: True. The warning protects the person, so it comes before the step.

feedback.text: Correct — a warning always precedes the step it protects.
No — the person must read the warning before doing the step.

name.text: L7 · Voicemail — exceptions to the rule

questiontext.text: Listen to the line supervisor's voicemail again. The new STE rule applies "without exception". How many exceptions are allowed?

generalfeedback.text: Zero. "From today, without exception, all reports must use Simplified Technical English."

feedback.text: Correct — "without exception" means zero exceptions.
"Without exception" means no exceptions — zero.

questiontext.text:
Read this task card.

TASK CARD 32-11-00 — Inspect the main gear bracket for corrosion. Clean the area. If the depth is within limits, tag the part serviceable. If the depth is not within limits, tag it unserviceable and raise a defect report.

What must the technician do if the corrosion depth is not within limits?

generalfeedback.text: Out of limits means the part is unserviceable, and a defect report must be raised.

answer.text: Tag it unserviceable and raise a defect report.

feedback.text: Correct — the card says exactly this.

answer.text: Clean the area, refit the panel, and close the work order.

feedback.text: No — the work order is not closed on an out-of-limits fault.

answer.text: Record the depth in the tech log and continue the check.

feedback.text: No — an out-of-limits part must be tagged and reported.

questiontext.text:
Read this MEL entry.

MEL 34-12 — The number two weather radar may be inoperative for up to 10 days. Placard the unit. Deactivate it in accordance with the procedure.

The MEL allows the number two weather radar to stay inoperative for a maximum of ten days.

generalfeedback.text: True. "up to 10 days" is the maximum allowed by this MEL item.

feedback.text: Correct — up to 10 days.
Re-read: the entry says "up to 10 days".

questiontext.text:
Read this Airworthiness Directive.

AD-2024-07 — Within the next 100 flight hours, inspect the rudder PCU bracket for cracks. This AD is mandatory. Report any crack to the manufacturer.

Within how many flight hours must the inspection be done? (Type the number.)

generalfeedback.text: 100 flight hours. The AD sets a hard interval, and it is mandatory.

feedback.text: Correct — within the next 100 flight hours.
The AD says within the next 100 flight hours.

questiontext.text:
Read this Service Bulletin note.

SB-27-1145 is recommended, unless your authority makes it mandatory. It affects the rudder PCU bracket.

A Service Bulletin is always mandatory.

generalfeedback.text: False. A Service Bulletin is recommended unless the authority makes it mandatory; an Airworthiness Directive is what is always mandatory.

feedback.text: No — a SB is recommended unless the authority makes it mandatory.
Correct — a SB is not automatically mandatory.

questiontext.text:
Read this work order.

WO-5567 — Replace the corroded antenna bracket. WARNING: isolate the electrical supply before removal. Close the work order only when the new bracket is fitted and tested.

When may the work order be closed?

generalfeedback.text: The work order stays open until the new bracket is fitted and tested.

answer.text: When the new bracket is fitted and tested.

feedback.text: Correct — those are the conditions stated on the work order.

answer.text: As soon as the electrical supply has been isolated.

feedback.text: No — isolating the supply is a warning step, not completion.

answer.text: After the warning has been written into the tech log.

feedback.text: No — the job must be finished and tested first.

questiontext.text:
Type the missing article.
The technician found ___ crack in the panel.

generalfeedback.text: a — a crack is mentioned for the first time, so use a. (Later: measure the crack.)

feedback.text: Correct — first mention takes a.
Not yet — the crack is new information, so use a first.
First mention of a countable noun takes a.

questiontext.text:
Type the article, or write none if no article is needed.
Check for ___ corrosion.

generalfeedback.text: none — "corrosion" is uncountable and general here, so it takes no article.

feedback.text: Correct — general uncountable, no article.
Correct — no article for a general uncountable noun.
Correct — no article needed.
No — "the corrosion" would mean a specific, already-known patch.
General uncountable nouns take no article.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite this heavy line as one short STE command in the active voice.
"The removal of the bolt should be done."

generalfeedback.text: Remove the bolt. Start with a technical verb, use the active voice, keep the article.

feedback.text: Correct — technical verb, active voice, article in place.
Correct — a full stop would finish it neatly.
Almost — do not drop the article: write "Remove the bolt."
Use the technical verb: "Remove the bolt."

name.text: U4 · Bank term — state of a part

questiontext.text:
Type the approved word.
A part that is not safe to use is ___ .

generalfeedback.text: unserviceable — the approved opposite of serviceable. Never write "bad" or "not okay".

feedback.text: Correct — the approved word for not safe to use.
That is the opposite — serviceable means safe to use.
The approved word is "unserviceable".

name.text: U5 · Bank term — safety note for people

questiontext.text:
Type the approved word.
The safety note that protects a person is a ___ .

generalfeedback.text: warning protects a person; a caution protects the part. Both go before the step.

feedback.text: Correct — a warning is for people.
No — a caution protects the part; a warning protects the person.
A warning protects a person from injury.

questiontext.text:
Type the missing article.
Find a crack. Measure ___ crack.

generalfeedback.text: the — the crack is now known (it was mentioned before), so use the.

feedback.text: Correct — second mention takes the.
No — the crack is already known, so use the.
Once a thing is known, use the.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: defect report = formal record; shift note = quick personal note; ambiguity = two meanings; warning = protects a person; caution = protects the part.

answer.text: A short, formal record of a fault.
When a sentence has two meanings.
A note that protects a person.
A note that protects the part.

name.text: V2 · Match term to its collocation

questiontext.text: Match each term to the word that usually goes with it.

generalfeedback.text: raise a defect report · close the work order · surface corrosion · sign the tech log · mounting bracket.

questiontext.text: Which is the approved STE word for a part that is not safe to use?

generalfeedback.text: "unserviceable" is the single approved word. Everyday phrases add ambiguity and are not allowed.

feedback.text: Correct — the one approved word.

answer.text: not really okay to fly it

feedback.text: No — an everyday phrase, not an approved word.

answer.text: a bit dodgy near the bolt

feedback.text: No — vague and not approved; it adds ambiguity.

questiontext.text: "Serviceable" means the part is not safe to use.

generalfeedback.text: False. Serviceable means in limits and safe to use. The opposite is unserviceable.

feedback.text: No — that is "unserviceable".
Correct — serviceable means safe to use.
